Before you begin.

Stop taking photos on the card.
New photos can overwrite missing data.

What can CardMe recover?

CardMe checks damaged JPEG photos and saves what it can recover, including smaller previews when the original is unavailable. It can also search for JPEG photos after deletion or a quick format, when the photo data is still intact. Recovery isn’t guaranteed.

Will it change anything on my card?

No. CardMe opens the card only for reading. It saves recovered photos and any safety copy to another drive. It doesn’t repair, format, or write to your card.

Why might it make a copy of the whole card?

For a deeper search, CardMe reads the whole card into a safety copy and recovers from that copy. You’ll need more free space than the card’s total capacity, plus room for the recovered photos. Larger cards take longer to copy.

What is currently not supported?

RAW photo recovery and general reconstruction of photos scattered across different parts of the card are currently not supported. Overwritten data cannot be recovered.

What usage information is shared?

Usage statistics are enabled by default. CardMe sends app opens, rescue result counts and coffee-link clicks, without an installation ID, photo names, paths or card details. You can turn this off in CardMe Settings. Reports are normally kept for 90 days; hosting services may retain network request metadata. Recovery works offline.

Are my photos uploaded?

No. Scanning and recovery happen on your Mac. You don’t need an account, and your photos aren’t uploaded.
